newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian commission starts work on welfare overview.
newsitem.headline: Italian commission starts work on welfare overview.

text.p: A commission set up to study the compatibility between welfare reform and policies aimed at boosting the economy met for the first time on Wednesday, the prime minister's office said in a statement.
The statement said the commission was expected to report its findings to Prime Minister Romano Prodi by February 28.

The centre-left government wants to reform social spending and Prodi said last week that the welfare state had to be realigned to changed conditions after decades of Italians "living beyond our means" by deficit spending.

The hard-left Communist Refoundation party, which lies outside Prodi's minority coalition and guarantees its majority in the lower house of parliament, backs welfare reform but wants no cut in the overall social spending budget.
Party leader Fausto Bertinotti told La Stampa newspaper on Wednesday that if anything, Italy should spend more on benefits.
"Welfare spending in Italy is less...than the European Union average," Bertinotti said. He said that old age pensions could not be touched but said the so-called baby pensions might be reviewed.
Baby pensions are given to state workers who were allowed to retire well before the usual pensionable age. They are now being phased out.
A government official told Reuters that the Treasury was considering hitting baby-pensions with a one-off solidarity tax later this year as part of a mini-budget. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
